mnist_rotated_matching.description: Paper Table 1, MNIST digits (10 classes): one image set is randomly rotated (uniform 0-360 degrees), the other is a disjoint unrotated set; is the transport plan class-preserving despite the rotations?

class_preservation_accuracy.description: Paper Table 1 quantity: fraction of source images whose transported mass, summed per target class, is largest on their own class. Recomputed by the evaluator from the submitted coupling.

same_class_mass_mean.description: Mean fraction of each source image's transported mass that lands on targets of its own class (soft class preservation, in [0, 1]).

class_mass_margin_mean.description: Mean of (own-class mass - strongest other-class mass) per source image, in [-1, 1]; separates confident from barely-correct correspondences.

mnist_rotated_matching._results_note: method = the paper's Bispectral OT (L1 ground cost, Greenkhorn, reg 0.01) scored by the hidden test; raw_ot_l1 = raw-pixel OT with L1 cost computed by the evaluator itself on the same instances.
mnist_rotated_matching._scale_note: Gym scale: each hidden-test instance has 100 images per class on each side (MNIST/KMNIST/FMNIST 1,000 x 1,000; EMNIST 2,600 x 2,600), two independent instances per experiment, drawn from the held-out t10k split. The paper matches two halves of the full training split (about 3,000 images per class per side), so its numbers, kept unchanged under _paper_results, are not on this scale and are not targets; `results` holds the gym-scale reference.

mnist_unrotated_baseline.description: Paper Table 1 control, MNIST digits (10 classes): both disjoint image sets are unrotated; checks that rotation robustness is not bought by destroying ordinary matching. The solver is not told which condition it faces.
